history: Found as a three-way split at the file-reading seam, one level ABOVE every limit any parser checks. Python and Rust refused at the decoder; the npm CLI and the verify page both substituted U+FFFD and went on to verify the result, so three distinct files shared one claim hash (c856f23670aa3692..) in the two implementations a stranger is most likely to reach. Both JavaScript sides now decode strictly.
note: The collision half of 008, and the reason it mattered. These bytes are a different FILE from 008's -- 0x80 rather than 0xFF, and 0xC3 is a third -- and a lenient decoder turns all three into the same U+FFFD, the same canonical form and the same receipt_sha256. canonical.py names exactly this property when it explains allow_nan=False: permitting NaN 'would let two different receipts share a canonical form'. Refusing all three satisfies the property outright; loading them with distinct hashes would too. Only loading them and agreeing on one hash is the failure, and that is what these two vectors rule out.
